IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.793 of 2026
Smt Jyoti Thapliyal ... Revisionist.
Versus
Mayank Bhatt ... Respondent.
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Dheeraj Joshi, learned counsel for the revisionist.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J. (Oral)
By means of the present Criminal Revision, the
revisionist has assailed the order dated 07.08.2026, passed
by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun, by means of
which the application for interim maintenance has been
rejected.
2. The proceedings of the case emanates out of an
application under Section 144 of the BNSS, by which, an
amount of ₹40,000 per month has been sought as
maintenance against the husband/respondent. Along with
the maintenance application, an application for interim
maintenance was also filed by the revisionist. The interim
maintenance application has been rejected by the Principal
Judge, Family Court, Dehradun on the ground that the
revisionist had left the matrimonial home and at the time of
leaving the matrimonial home had given a letter dated
19.01.2023 stating that she is leaving the matrimonial home
on her own without any pressure, and her mother and
brother are with her, and she is also taking along valuable
jewellery. The ceremonial ring has been left back, and she
would further reside in her maika in Sauda Saroli, Raipur.
Another document relied upon by the learned Principal
Judge, Family Court, Dehradun is an assurance letter, which
1

was filed along with her affidavit of assets and liabilities, in
which the revisionist had stated that in future she will have
no concern with Rohit Rawat and in future she will not
contact him, nor will she meet him physically. If such a thing
happens, the entire responsibility will be of the revisionist
and her parents. The said document has been written by her
in her senses without any pressure.
3. Based on the aforesaid two documents, the
learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun has come
to a conclusion that the revisionist has no plausible reason
for living separately from her husband, and it appears that
she is living away and that she has deserted her in-laws'
place and is residing in her maika on her own free will.
4. The learned Principal Judge, Family Court,
Dehradun has further inferred that there is no reasonable
ground proved by the revisionist and it appears that the
revisionist is residing in her maika separately from the
husband on her own. Relying upon Section 144(4) of the
BNSS, the application for interim maintenance has been
rejected.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist would submit
that the documents relied upon by the learned Principal
Judge, Family Court, Dehradun were written/submitted by
the revisionist under duress, and such a document cannot be
taken into consideration for any purpose whatsoever. Later
on, before the Women's Cell, the revisionist expressed her
desire to live with her husband, however, the
husband/respondent refused to take along the wife.
6. On such grounds, the learned counsel for the
applicant urges the Court to allow the Criminal Revision.
7. After considering the submissions advanced by
the learned counsel for the revisionist and going through the
record, the impugned order dated 07.08.2026, passed by the
Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun is based on certain
2

UKHC010181502026
2026:UHC:9414
documents which reflect that the revisionist is residing in her
maika on her own will and she has deserted her in-laws'
place. This Court, after going through the record and the
impugned order, does not find any infirmity or jurisdictional
error in the impugned order. However, the reasons so relied
upon by the learned Principal Judge, Family Court,
Dehradun may be reasons to reject the application for interim
maintenance.
8. Learned counsel for the revisionist urges the Court
that these particular documents relied upon by the learned
Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun may not come in
the way of the final adjudication of the application under
Section 144 of the BNSS.
9. The case under Section 144 of the BNSS is at its
initial stage. Therefore, there is no scope for interference in
the present Criminal Revision.
10. The Criminal Revision is accordingly dismissed
with the observation that any finding recorded in the
impugned order dated 07.08.2026 will not come in the way of
the final adjudication of the application under Section 144 of
the BNSS, and the same shall be decided finally on its own
merit without being influenced by the findings recorded in the
impugned order.
11. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of
accordingly.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.)
14.10.2026
Shiv/
